title: NOx Sensor Bank 2 Range/Performance (P204D)
shortDescription: NOx sensor bank 2 range/performance fault stored as P204D.
fullDescription: The PCM has detected the bank-2 NOx sensor signal outside expected range under steady-state conditions. Code P204D typically points to the downstream/feedback sensor or its heater.
safetyImpact: Failure can trigger emissions limp mode and reduced power, which may surprise the driver in traffic.

causes.cause: Wiring or connector corrosion at sensor

symptoms: Reduced engine power / limp mode countdown

fixSteps.title: Scan Live Data
fixSteps.instruction: Compare upstream and downstream NOx sensor readings during steady cruise. Healthy SCR shows >70% reduction.

fixSteps.title: Inspect DEF Quality
fixSteps.instruction: Test DEF refractive index (32.5% urea). Replace fluid and flush tank if contaminated.

fixSteps.title: Check Sensor Wiring
fixSteps.instruction: Inspect harness for chafing near exhaust heat shields. Repair or replace as needed.

fixSteps.title: Replace NOx Sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Replace the affected NOx sensor with an OEM unit and clear adaptations.

faq.q: Can I drive with this code?
faq.a: Short trips are usually allowed, but most diesels begin a limp-mode countdown that limits speed within a few starts.

faq.q: Is the NOx sensor expensive?
faq.a: Yes — OEM NOx sensors typically run $300–$700, plus labor.

title: DEF/SCR Reductant System (P207A)
shortDescription: Diesel exhaust fluid / SCR feedback fault stored as P207A.
fullDescription: The reductant control system reports a fault — usually quality, dosing, or NOx reduction efficiency — under code P207A. Many platforms begin a derate/no-start countdown.
safetyImpact: Diesel emissions faults trigger derate strategies that limit power and speed, posing risk in highway driving.

causes.cause: DEF tank contamination or wrong fluid
Exhaust leak between SCR and tailpipe sensor

symptoms: Check engine light with DEF warning

fixSteps.title: Confirm DEF Quality and Level
fixSteps.instruction: Verify DEF concentration with a refractometer; top up only with API-certified DEF.

fixSteps.title: Read SCR Live Data
fixSteps.instruction: Monitor NOx in/out, DEF dosing rate, and SCR temperature during a forced regen.

fixSteps.title: Inspect Dosing Module
fixSteps.instruction: Check DEF injector spray pattern and DEF lines for crystallization.

fixSteps.title: Service SCR System
fixSteps.instruction: Replace failed sensor, dosing valve, or SCR catalyst as indicated by data.

faq.q: Why does the truck threaten to not start?
faq.a: Federal regulations require diesel SCR systems to derate and eventually inhibit start when emissions controls are inoperative.

faq.q: Will adding more DEF clear it?
faq.a: Only if the cause is a low or empty DEF tank. Contaminated fluid must be drained and replaced.

title: NOx Adsorber Catalyst Efficiency (P209A)
shortDescription: NOx adsorber efficiency or temperature out of range — P209A.
fullDescription: The NOx storage catalyst is not regenerating or storing within the expected window. Code P209A can indicate sulfur poisoning, sensor disagreement, or an aged substrate.
safetyImpact: Catalyst faults rarely affect handling but eventually trigger reduced power that can surprise the driver.

causes.cause: NOx adsorber catalyst saturated or aged
Failed regen due to low EGT
Faulty NOx or temperature sensor feedback

fixSteps.title: Verify Regen Conditions
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm vehicle has driven long enough at highway load for adsorber regen to complete.

fixSteps.title: Run Forced Desulfation
fixSteps.instruction: Use OEM scan tool to command a high-temperature desulfation cycle.

fixSteps.title: Check Sensors
fixSteps.instruction: Validate upstream/downstream NOx and EGT sensor readings against spec.

fixSteps.title: Replace Catalyst
fixSteps.instruction: If desulfation fails, replace the NOx adsorber/SCR assembly with an OEM part.

faq.q: Can a fuel additive fix this?
faq.a: Cleaners may help mild sulfur poisoning, but a saturated or cracked catalyst must be replaced.

faq.q: Is desulfation safe to do repeatedly?
faq.a: Occasional desulfation is normal; frequent cycles indicate fuel quality or sensor problems that should be diagnosed.

title: Crankcase Pressure Sensor Circuit (P226A)
shortDescription: Crankcase pressure sensor circuit fault stored as P226A.
fullDescription: The crankcase pressure / PCV sensor signal is implausible. Code P226A may indicate sensor failure, plugged PCV, or excessive blow-by.
safetyImpact: Oil leaks from positive crankcase pressure can foul the engine bay and, in worst cases, reach hot exhaust.
symptoms: Oil leaks from gaskets / dipstick tube
Smoke from oil filler when running

fixSteps.title: Inspect PCV System
fixSteps.instruction: Check PCV valve operation and hoses for cracks; replace as necessary.

fixSteps.title: Measure Crankcase Pressure
fixSteps.instruction: Use a low-pressure manometer at the oil filler to compare with spec (usually slight vacuum).

fixSteps.title: Test the Sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Backprobe sensor signal and compare to scan-tool PID across RPM range.

fixSteps.title: Repair Source
fixSteps.instruction: Replace failed PCV components or sensor; investigate blow-by if pressure is high.

faq.q: Can high crankcase pressure damage seals?
faq.a: Yes — sustained positive pressure pushes oil past every seal in the engine.

faq.q: Will a catch can fix this?
faq.a: A catch can helps with oil mist but does not solve a stuck PCV or worn rings.

fullDescription: The crankcase pressure / PCV sensor signal is implausible. Code P2270 may indicate sensor failure, plugged PCV, or excessive blow-by.
safetyImpact: Oil leaks from positive crankcase pressure can foul the engine bay and, in worst cases, reach hot exhaust.
symptoms: Oil leaks from gaskets / dipstick tube
Smoke from oil filler when running

fixSteps.title: Inspect PCV System
fixSteps.instruction: Check PCV valve operation and hoses for cracks; replace as necessary.

fixSteps.title: Measure Crankcase Pressure
fixSteps.instruction: Use a low-pressure manometer at the oil filler to compare with spec (usually slight vacuum).

fixSteps.title: Test the Sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Backprobe sensor signal and compare to scan-tool PID across RPM range.

fixSteps.title: Repair Source
fixSteps.instruction: Replace failed PCV components or sensor; investigate blow-by if pressure is high.

faq.q: Can high crankcase pressure damage seals?
faq.a: Yes — sustained positive pressure pushes oil past every seal in the engine.

faq.q: Will a catch can fix this?
faq.a: A catch can helps with oil mist but does not solve a stuck PCV or worn rings.

title: Lambda Sensor Multibank Slow Response (P2A00)
shortDescription: Lambda sensor multibank performance fault — P2A00.
fullDescription: The PCM evaluates lambda sensor response across multiple banks and reports P2A00 when transitions are slower than spec or banks disagree under steady conditions.
safetyImpact: Long-running mixture errors can damage catalysts and, in extreme cases, raise exhaust temperatures.

fixSteps.title: Read Lambda Live Data
fixSteps.instruction: Compare bank 1 vs bank 2 wideband signals during cruise; both should track ~1.0 with light variation.

fixSteps.title: Inspect Exhaust
fixSteps.instruction: Look for leaks at manifold gaskets and sensor bungs that lean out the upstream signal.

fixSteps.title: Check Heater Circuit
fixSteps.instruction: Verify heater resistance and 12V supply; a slow-warming sensor sets multibank faults.

fixSteps.title: Replace Sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Install OEM lambda sensor on affected bank, clear adaptations, and re-evaluate.

faq.q: Do I need to replace both bank sensors?
faq.a: Not always — replace what data points to. If both are original and one fails, the other is often close behind.

faq.q: Will fuel additive help?
faq.a: Only if a fouling agent (silicone, leaded race fuel) was the cause. Most lambda failures are sensor wear.
